av_event.line_text: Ha, fair. The whisky makes up for it. And the seals. There was this one seal that followed us along the beach for about a mile, and Joe was convinced it wanted his sandwich. Sorry, I'm rambling, go on.
av_event.what: While Rachel is talking, the Apple Watch on Nicola's raised wrist lights up. Nicola drops her eyes to it and reads it for a couple of seconds, then looks back at the screen with the same half-smile.

text:
B: Hiya! Hello, can you hear me? I'm Rachel.
A: Yep, loud and clear. Nicola. Where are you?
B: Lancaster. You?
A: Woodley, near Reading. Third one of these now, I'm getting the hang of it.
B: Same, I've had two lovely chats already, so no pressure on you. Erm, what do you do?
A: SAP consultant. Finance systems. Nobody ever knows what that is, so basically, big companies move their accounts onto new software and I make it work. I'm on a contract in Bracknell, logistics firm, and honestly it's held together with Sellotape. Every meeting someone goes, oh, we've always done it on a spreadsheet, and I'm like, right, well, you can't now.
B: Oh God, I am that person. I'd be your worst nightmare. There's one shared spreadsheet at work and my colleague keeps it alive. I'm not really allowed to touch it.
A: Ha, sensible. What is it you do, then?
B: I work at an arts centre. Participation and events, so community workshops, family days, a bit of touring theatre. This week I've had a group of teenagers doing a devised piece about the bus station. It sounds awful, but it was actually brilliant, you know? One lad who never speaks did this whole monologue about his nan and the room just went silent.
A: Right. Is that, like, council funded?
B: Partly. Arts Council, bits from trusts. My post's only funded for another eighteen months, so, yeah. Trying not to think about it.
A: That's the thing with funded stuff though, isn't it, it's always hand to mouth. You should go freelance. Honestly, best thing I ever did. You set your rate and you're not waiting on some committee.
B: I'd be terrible at the invoicing. I've got about nine hundred unread emails.
A: Nine hundred? Oh my God. I'd have a breakdown.
B: I sort of just let them sit there and judge me. Sorry, what do you do when you're not working? Have you got time?
A: Padel, mostly. Once a week at a club in Reading. Do you know padel?
B: Is that the one that's like tennis in a cage?
A: Sort of. Smaller court, glass walls, you can play off them. It's addictive. My partner keeps double-faulting though, which is driving me mad. I've said to her, we're not winning the league if you keep doing that.
B: You play in a league? I did couch to 5k twice and quit both times at week four.
A: Week four's where it gets hard, to be fair.
B: That's what everyone says! Do you go away much? I was just talking about Lisbon with someone.
A: Lisbon's nice. I did a long weekend there with the girls. Mostly I like somewhere hot where someone brings you a drink. Mauritius last year with my son, Dubai before that.
B: Ooh. I'm more trains and walking. I did a week on Islay and it rained every single day and I loved it.
A: Every day? No, you've lost me there. I need sun. So, yeah.
B: Ha, fair. The whisky makes up for it. And the seals. There was this one seal that followed us along the beach for about a mile, and Joe was convinced it wanted his sandwich. Sorry, I'm rambling, go on.
A: No, you're alright. Have you got kids? I saw a kid's drawing on your board.
B: Oh, no, that's from a family day. A little girl drew me as a dragon, I was made up. We haven't got kids. Joe and I are sort of talking about it, you know?
A: Take your time, is my advice. Mine's fifteen, he's got his mocks and he won't revise. Lives on his phone.
B: Were those his trainers in your hall, in your picture?
A: Probably, he leaves them everywhere. My cleaner moves them, and then
